title: Number Sentences: Equations, Balances and Substitution
seo_title: Grade 6 Number Sentences Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Write number sentences to describe problem situations; analyse and interpret number sentences that describe a given situation; solve and complete number sentences by inspection and by trial and improvement; check solutions by substitution.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 number sentences worksheets: balances, missing numbers, letters for unknowns, substitution and writing number sentences. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Use inverse operations, in reverse order.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A number sentence uses = to show both sides have the same value: 3 × ☐ + 4 = 25.
  • Use inverse operations to find the missing number: 25 − 4 = 21, 21 ÷ 3 = 7.
  • A letter can stand for the missing number: y − 38 = 64, so y = 102.
  • Check by substitution: put the number back in and see if both sides are equal.

Examples

Example

4 × n − 6 = 30

30 + 6 = 36

36 ÷ 4

Answer: n = 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The same operationUse the inverse.
One side onlyKeep the balance level.
Wrong operationRead what the story does.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about number sentences?
faq.a: Write number sentences to describe problem situations, solve and complete number sentences by inspection and trial and improvement, and check solutions by substitution.
Putting a number in place of the letter to check.
A number sentence with an = sign.
Yes, then there can be many solutions.

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: The pans balance, so both sides are equal. Write what is on each pan with = between them: x + 12 = 30. Then x = 18.

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: There are 4 blocks x on one pan. 4 equal blocks is 4x, which means 4 × x. So 4x = 28. Then x = 7.

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: The pans balance, so both sides are equal. Write what is on each pan with = between them: 45 = y + 19. Then y = 26.

items.q: The pans balance. Which equation matches?
items.e: There are 5 blocks n on one pan. 5 equal blocks is 5n, which means 5 × n. So 5n = 30 + 15. Then n = 9.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, x. What is x?
items.e: The balance shows x + 25 = 60. Subtract 25 from both sides: x = 60 − 25 = 35. Check: 35 + 25 = 60. Wrong answers: 85 comes from adding 25 instead of subtracting it; 45 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, m. What is m?
items.e: The balance shows 3m = 21. 3m means 3 × m. Divide both sides by 3: m = 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Check: 3 × 7 = 21. Wrong answers: 18 comes from subtracting 3 instead of dividing; 63 comes from multiplying by 3 instead of dividing.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, k. What is k?
items.e: The balance shows k + 140 = 500. Subtract 140 from both sides: k = 500 − 140 = 360. Check: 360 + 140 = 500. Wrong answers: 640 comes from adding 140 instead of subtracting it; 440 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, a. What is a?
items.e: The balance shows 6a = 54. 6a means 6 × a. Divide both sides by 6: a = 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Check: 6 × 9 = 54. Wrong answers: 48 comes from subtracting 6 instead of dividing; 324 comes from multiplying by 6 instead of dividing.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, p. What is p?
items.e: The balance shows 72 = p + 38. Subtract 38 from both sides: p = 72 − 38 = 34. Check: 34 + 38 = 72. Wrong answers: 110 comes from adding 38 instead of subtracting it; 46 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, y. What is y?
items.e: The right pan has 14 + 20 = 34. So y + 9 = 34. Subtract 9 from both sides: y = 34 − 9 = 25. Check: 25 + 9 = 34. Wrong answers: 43 comes from adding 9 instead of subtracting it; 35 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, t. What is t?
items.e: The right pan has 40 + 16 = 56. So 2t = 56. 2t means 2 × t. Divide both sides by 2: t = 56 ÷ 2 = 28. Check: 2 × 28 = 56. Wrong answers: 54 comes from subtracting 2 instead of dividing; 112 comes from multiplying by 2 instead of dividing.

items.q: The balance shows x + 12 = 30. You take 12 off the left pan. What must you do to the right pan to keep it level?
items.e: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other side. Take 12 off the right pan too: x = 30 − 12 = 18. Adding 12 to the right pan would make it tip.

items.q: The balance shows 4x = 28. To find one block, you split the left pan into 4 equal groups. What must you do to the right side?
items.e: Do the same to both sides. Split both sides into 4 equal groups: 28 ÷ 4 = 7, so x = 7. Subtracting 4 undoes + 4, not × 4.

items.q: Which step solves x − 9 = 20 and keeps both sides equal?
items.e: Adding undoes subtracting. Add 9 to both sides: x = 20 + 9 = 29. Check: 29 − 9 = 20. Subtracting 9 again is the same operation, not the inverse.

items.q: Which step solves x ÷ 5 = 6 and keeps both sides equal?
items.e: Multiplying undoes dividing. Multiply both sides by 5: x = 6 × 5 = 30. Check: 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Dividing by 5 again is the same operation.

items.q: Which equation has the solution x = 6?
items.e: Substitute x = 6 into each equation. 7 × 6 = 42, so 7x = 42 is true. 6x = 6 has the solution 1.

items.q: Which equation has the solution x = 12?
items.e: Substitute x = 12 into each equation. 12 − 4 = 8, so x − 4 = 8 is true. x ÷ 4 = 8 has the solution 32.

items.q: Which equation has the solution x = 40?
items.e: Substitute x = 40 into each equation. 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so x ÷ 5 = 8 is true. 8x = 40 has the solution 5, not 40: it mixes up the two numbers.

items.q: What does 5x mean?
items.e: A number written right before a letter means multiply. 5x means 5 × x, or 5 equal blocks of x. If x = 7, then 5x = 35.

items.q: Kyle solves x + 12 = 30 and gets x = 42. Which check shows that his answer is wrong?
items.e: To check, put the answer back into the equation: 42 + 12 = 54, and 54 is not 30. Kyle added 12 instead of subtracting it. The right answer is 30 − 12 = 18.

items.q: Solve x + 12 = 30. What is x?
items.e: Subtract 12 from both sides: x = 30 − 12 = 18. Check: 18 + 12 = 30. Wrong answers: 42 comes from adding 12 instead of subtracting it; 22 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve x + 27 = 64. What is x?
items.e: Subtract 27 from both sides: x = 64 − 27 = 37. Check: 37 + 27 = 64. Wrong answers: 91 comes from adding 27 instead of subtracting it; 43 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve 45 + n = 91. What is n?
items.e: Subtract 45 from both sides: n = 91 − 45 = 46. Check: 45 + 46 = 91. Wrong answers: 136 comes from adding 45 instead of subtracting it; 54 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve y + 138 = 405. What is y?
items.e: Subtract 138 from both sides: y = 405 − 138 = 267. Check: 267 + 138 = 405. Wrong answers: 543 comes from adding 138 instead of subtracting it; 333 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve x − 15 = 40. What is x?
items.e: Add 15 to both sides: x = 40 + 15 = 55. Check: 55 − 15 = 40. Wrong answers: 25 comes from subtracting 15 again instead of adding it.

items.q: Solve m − 48 = 75. What is m?
items.e: Add 48 to both sides: m = 75 + 48 = 123. Check: 123 − 48 = 75. Wrong answers: 27 comes from subtracting 48 again instead of adding it; 13 comes from forgetting to carry.

items.q: Solve a − 250 = 380. What is a?
items.e: Add 250 to both sides: a = 380 + 250 = 630. Check: 630 − 250 = 380. Wrong answers: 130 comes from subtracting 250 again instead of adding it; 530 comes from forgetting to carry.

items.q: Solve 84 = x + 29. What is x?
items.e: Subtract 29 from both sides: x = 84 − 29 = 55. Check: 55 + 29 = 84. Wrong answers: 113 comes from adding 29 instead of subtracting it; 65 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve 120 = p − 65. What is p?
items.e: Add 65 to both sides: p = 120 + 65 = 185. Check: 185 − 65 = 120. Wrong answers: 55 comes from subtracting 65 again instead of adding it.

items.q: Solve 90 − x = 34. What is x?
items.e: 90 take away what leaves 34? x = 90 − 34 = 56. Check: 90 − 56 = 34. Wrong answers: 124 comes from adding the two numbers; 64 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve 500 − y = 215. What is y?
items.e: 500 take away what leaves 215? y = 500 − 215 = 285. Check: 500 − 285 = 215. Wrong answers: 715 comes from adding the two numbers; 315 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve 1 500 + x = 4 200. What is x?
items.e: Subtract 1 500 from both sides: x = 4 200 − 1 500 = 2 700. Check: 1 500 + 2 700 = 4 200. Wrong answers: 5 700 comes from adding 1 500 instead of subtracting it; 3 300 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve x + 2 750 = 6 000. What is x?
items.e: Subtract 2 750 from both sides: x = 6 000 − 2 750 = 3 250. Check: 3 250 + 2 750 = 6 000. Wrong answers: 8 750 comes from adding 2 750 instead of subtracting it; 4 750 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve k − 1 800 = 3 600. What is k?
items.e: Add 1 800 to both sides: k = 3 600 + 1 800 = 5 400. Check: 5 400 − 1 800 = 3 600. Wrong answers: 1 800 comes from subtracting 1 800 again instead of adding it; 4 400 comes from forgetting to carry.

items.q: Solve x + 12 500 = 30 000. What is x?
items.e: Subtract 12 500 from both sides: x = 30 000 − 12 500 = 17 500. Check: 17 500 + 12 500 = 30 000. Wrong answers: 42 500 comes from adding 12 500 instead of subtracting it; 22 500 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Solve n − 25 000 = 48 000. What is n?
items.e: Add 25 000 to both sides: n = 48 000 + 25 000 = 73 000. Check: 73 000 − 25 000 = 48 000. Wrong answers: 23 000 comes from subtracting 25 000 again instead of adding it; 63 000 comes from forgetting to carry.

items.q: Solve x + 45 000 = 120 000. What is x?
items.e: Subtract 45 000 from both sides: x = 120 000 − 45 000 = 75 000. Check: 75 000 + 45 000 = 120 000. Wrong answers: 165 000 comes from adding 45 000 instead of subtracting it; 125 000 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

Subtract 2 500 000 from both sides: d = 7 000 000 − 2 500 000 = 4 500 000. Check: 4 500 000 + 2 500 000 = 7 000 000. Wrong answers: 9 500 000 comes from adding 2 500 000 instead of subtracting it; 5 500 000 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Ethan solves x − 25 = 40 and gets x = 15. What did he do wrong?
items.e: Check: 15 − 25 does not give 40. He used the same operation, subtraction, instead of the inverse. Add 25 to both sides: x = 40 + 25 = 65. Check: 65 − 25 = 40.

items.q: What is the first step to solve x + 38 = 95?
items.e: Subtraction undoes addition. Subtract 38 from both sides: x = 95 − 38 = 57. Check: 57 + 38 = 95.

items.q: Solve 5x = 35. What is x?
items.e: 5x means 5 × x. Divide both sides by 5: x = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Check: 5 × 7 = 35. Wrong answers: 30 comes from subtracting 5 instead of dividing; 175 comes from multiplying by 5 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 3n = 27. What is n?
items.e: 3n means 3 × n. Divide both sides by 3: n = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Check: 3 × 9 = 27. Wrong answers: 24 comes from subtracting 3 instead of dividing; 81 comes from multiplying by 3 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 8y = 56. What is y?
items.e: 8y means 8 × y. Divide both sides by 8: y = 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Check: 8 × 7 = 56. Wrong answers: 48 comes from subtracting 8 instead of dividing; 448 comes from multiplying by 8 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 9m = 72. What is m?
items.e: 9m means 9 × m. Divide both sides by 9: m = 72 ÷ 9 = 8. Check: 9 × 8 = 72. Wrong answers: 63 comes from subtracting 9 instead of dividing; 648 comes from multiplying by 9 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 6x = 54. What is x?
items.e: 6x means 6 × x. Divide both sides by 6: x = 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Check: 6 × 9 = 54. Wrong answers: 48 comes from subtracting 6 instead of dividing; 324 comes from multiplying by 6 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 7k = 84. What is k?
items.e: 7k means 7 × k. Divide both sides by 7: k = 84 ÷ 7 = 12. Check: 7 × 12 = 84. Wrong answers: 77 comes from subtracting 7 instead of dividing; 588 comes from multiplying by 7 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 12x = 96. What is x?
items.e: 12x means 12 × x. Divide both sides by 12: x = 96 ÷ 12 = 8. Check: 12 × 8 = 96. Wrong answers: 84 comes from subtracting 12 instead of dividing; 1 152 comes from multiplying by 12 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 11p = 132. What is p?
items.e: 11p means 11 × p. Divide both sides by 11: p = 132 ÷ 11 = 12. Check: 11 × 12 = 132. Wrong answers: 121 comes from subtracting 11 instead of dividing; 1 452 comes from multiplying by 11 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 63 = 7x. What is x?
items.e: 7x means 7 × x. Divide both sides by 7: x = 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Check: 7 × 9 = 63. Wrong answers: 56 comes from subtracting 7 instead of dividing; 441 comes from multiplying by 7 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve 120 = 8n. What is n?
items.e: 8n means 8 × n. Divide both sides by 8: n = 120 ÷ 8 = 15. Check: 8 × 15 = 120. Wrong answers: 112 comes from subtracting 8 instead of dividing; 960 comes from multiplying by 8 instead of dividing.

items.q: Solve x ÷ 4 = 8. What is x?
items.e: x is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 4: x = 8 × 4 = 32. Check: 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Wrong answers: 2 comes from dividing by 4 again instead of multiplying; 12 comes from adding 4 instead of multiplying; 4 comes from subtracting 4.

items.q: Solve n ÷ 3 = 9. What is n?
items.e: n is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 3: n = 9 × 3 = 27. Check: 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Wrong answers: 3 comes from dividing by 3 again instead of multiplying; 12 comes from adding 3 instead of multiplying; 6 comes from subtracting 3.

items.q: Solve y ÷ 6 = 7. What is y?
items.e: y is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 6: y = 7 × 6 = 42. Check: 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Wrong answers: 13 comes from adding 6 instead of multiplying; 1 comes from subtracting 6.

items.q: Solve m ÷ 5 = 12. What is m?
items.e: m is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 5: m = 12 × 5 = 60. Check: 60 ÷ 5 = 12. Wrong answers: 17 comes from adding 5 instead of multiplying; 7 comes from subtracting 5.

items.q: Solve x ÷ 8 = 9. What is x?
items.e: x is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 8: x = 9 × 8 = 72. Check: 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Wrong answers: 17 comes from adding 8 instead of multiplying; 1 comes from subtracting 8.

items.q: Solve k ÷ 12 = 7. What is k?
items.e: k is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 12: k = 7 × 12 = 84. Check: 84 ÷ 12 = 7. Wrong answers: 19 comes from adding 12 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Solve x ÷ 10 = 45. What is x?
items.e: x is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 10: x = 45 × 10 = 450. Check: 450 ÷ 10 = 45. Wrong answers: 55 comes from adding 10 instead of multiplying; 4 500 comes from a place-value slip with the zeros; 45 comes from a place-value slip with the zeros.

items.q: Solve p ÷ 25 = 4. What is p?
items.e: p is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 25: p = 4 × 25 = 100. Check: 100 ÷ 25 = 4. Wrong answers: 29 comes from adding 25 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Solve x ÷ 100 = 36. What is x?
items.e: x is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 100: x = 36 × 100 = 3 600. Check: 3 600 ÷ 100 = 36. Wrong answers: 136 comes from adding 100 instead of multiplying; 36 000 comes from a place-value slip with the zeros; 360 comes from a place-value slip with the zeros.

items.q: Solve x ÷ 1 000 = 250. What is x?
items.e: x is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 1 000: x = 250 × 1 000 = 250 000. Check: 250 000 ÷ 1 000 = 250. Wrong answers: 1 250 comes from adding 1 000 instead of multiplying; 2 500 000 comes from a place-value slip with the zeros; 25 000 comes from a place-value slip with the zeros.

items.q: Johan solved 2x + 9 = 31 and got x = 20. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Check: 2 × 20 + 9 = 49, not 31, so 20 is wrong. Using the wrong inverse operation gives 20. The right way: Subtract 9 from both sides: 2x = 22. Then divide both sides by 2: x = 22 ÷ 2 = 11. Check: 2 × 11 + 9 = 31.

items.q: Kgomotso solved 3x + 6 = 33 and got x = 5. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check: 3 × 5 + 6 = 21, not 33, so 5 is wrong. Undoing in the wrong order gives 5. The right way: Subtract 6 from both sides: 3x = 27. Then divide both sides by 3: x = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Check: 3 × 9 + 6 = 33.

items.q: Chloe solved 4x + 7 = 43 and got x = 36. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check: 4 × 36 + 7 = 151, not 43, so 36 is wrong. Stopping after the first step gives 36. The right way: Subtract 7 from both sides: 4x = 36. Then divide both sides by 4: x = 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Check: 4 × 9 + 7 = 43.

items.q: Priya solved 5x − 5 = 40 and got x = 7. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check: 5 × 7 − 5 = 30, not 40, so 7 is wrong. Using the wrong inverse operation gives 7. The right way: Add 5 to both sides: 5x = 45. Then divide both sides by 5: x = 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Check: 5 × 9 − 5 = 40.

items.q: Ofentse solved 6x − 3 = 45 and got x = 288. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check: 6 × 288 − 3 = 1 725, not 45, so 288 is wrong. Multiplying gives 288. The right way: Add 3 to both sides: 6x = 48. Then divide both sides by 6: x = 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 6 × 8 − 3 = 45.

items.q: Lungile solved 4x − 8 = 36 and got x = 17. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Check: 4 × 17 − 8 = 60, not 36, so 17 is wrong. Undoing in the wrong order gives 17. The right way: Add 8 to both sides: 4x = 44. Then divide both sides by 4: x = 44 ÷ 4 = 11. Check: 4 × 11 − 8 = 36.

items.q: Which work correctly checks that x = 9 is the solution of 4x − 6 = 30?
items.e: 4x means 4 × x. Multiply first, then subtract: 4 × 9 − 6 = 36 − 6 = 30. The left side equals 30, so x = 9 is correct.

items.q: Which work correctly checks that x = 7 is the solution of 5x + 8 = 43?
items.e: 5x means 5 × x. Multiply first, then add: 5 × 7 + 8 = 35 + 8 = 43. The left side equals 43, so x = 7 is correct.

items.q: Which work correctly checks that x = 11 is the solution of 3x + 7 = 40?
items.e: 3x means 3 × x. Multiply first, then add: 3 × 11 + 7 = 33 + 7 = 40. The left side equals 40, so x = 11 is correct.

items.q: Kagiso solved 2x + 9 = 31 and got x = 20. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Check: 2 × 20 + 9 = 49, not 31, so 20 is wrong. Using the wrong inverse operation gives 20. The right way: Subtract 9 from both sides: 2x = 22. Then divide both sides by 2: x = 22 ÷ 2 = 11. Check: 2 × 11 + 9 = 31.

items.q: If n = 4, what is the value of 3n?
items.e: 3n means 3 × n. So 3 × 4 = 12. It does not mean 34: the 3 and the n are multiplied, not written side by side.

items.q: If y = 9, what is y − 4?
items.e: Replace y with 9: 9 − 4 = 5. (13 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: If x = 4 and y = 7, what is xy?
items.e: xy means x × y. So 4 × 7 = 28. Not 47 (side by side) and not 11 (adding).

items.q: If a = 6, what is 2a + 5?
items.e: Multiply first: 2 × 6 = 12. Then add 5: 12 + 5 = 17. Not 31: 2a is not 26. Not 22: that adds 6 + 5 first.

items.q: If m = 5, what is 4m − 3?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20, then 20 − 3 = 17. Not 42: 4m is not 45. Not 8: that subtracts first, 4 × 2.

items.q: If k = 8, what is k ÷ 2 + 3?
items.e: Divide first: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Then add 3: 4 + 3 = 7. Not 1,6: that adds 2 + 3 first. Not 4: it forgets to add 3.

items.q: If p = 7, what is 20 − 2p?
items.e: Multiply first: 2 × 7 = 14. Then 20 − 14 = 6. Not 126: that does 20 − 2 = 18 first, then 18 × 7.

items.q: The perimeter of a square is P = 4s, where s is the length of a side. What is the perimeter of this square?
items.e: Replace s with 9: 4 × 9 = 36 cm. 81 cm multiplies 9 × 9, which is how you find the area. 13 cm adds 4 + 9. 49 cm reads 4s as 49.

items.q: A farmer uses ℓ = 4c to count the legs ℓ on c cows. How many legs do 12 cows have?
items.e: 4c means 4 × c. 4 × 12 = 48. Not 412: do not write the numbers side by side. Not 16: that adds 4 + 12.

items.q: To change metres to centimetres, use c = 100m, where c is centimetres and m is metres. How many centimetres are in 7 metres?
items.e: 100 × 7 = 700. There are 100 cm in 1 m. 107 adds, 70 multiplies by 10 and 7 000 multiplies by 1 000.

items.q: 4 SkyTrain cars carry 520 people. Each car carries the same number of people, p. Which equation matches?
items.e: 4 equal groups of p make 520: 4p = 520. Equal groups mean ×, not +. Then p = 520 ÷ 4 = 130.

items.q: Which equation means “a number divided by 7 is 15”?
items.e: Start with the number n and divide it by 7: n ÷ 7 = 15. Then n = 15 × 7 = 105. 7 ÷ n starts with 7, not with the number.

items.q: Which equation means “6 times a number is 84”?
items.e: “6 times a number” is 6n, and “is 84” is = 84: 6n = 84. Then n = 84 ÷ 6 = 14.

items.q: Which story matches x − 120 = 380?
c: 380 salmon swim up a creek and 120 are caught.
120 salmon swim up a creek and then 380 more come.
Some salmon swim up a creek. 120 are caught and 380 are left.
items.e: x is the number at the start. Take away 120 and 380 are left: x − 120 = 380. Then x = 380 + 120 = 500. The story “380 salmon … 120 are caught” starts with 380, so it matches 380 − 120 = x.

items.q: A stadium has 54 000 seats. 38 750 people are in their seats. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Equation: 38 750 + e = 54 000. Subtract 38 750 from both sides: e = 54 000 − 38 750 = 15 250. Check: 38 750 + 15 250 = 54 000. Wrong answers: 92 750 seats comes from adding 38 750 instead of subtracting it; 24 750 seats comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: Jabu cuts a 200 cm cedar board into 8 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Equation: 8p = 200. 8p means 8 × p. Divide both sides by 8: p = 200 ÷ 8 = 25. Check: 8 × 25 = 200. Wrong answers: 192 cm comes from subtracting 8 instead of dividing; 1 600 cm comes from multiplying by 8 instead of dividing.

items.q: The learners in a Grade 6 class form 4 equal lacrosse teams with 7 players on each team. How many learners are in the class?
items.e: Equation: s ÷ 4 = 7. s is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 4: s = 7 × 4 = 28. Check: 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Wrong answers: 11 learners comes from adding 4 instead of multiplying; 32 learners comes from 4 × 8, the wrong fact; 24 learners comes from 4 × 6, the wrong fact.

items.q: A school district plans to plant 10 000 tree seedlings. Learners have planted 6 475 so far. How many more do they need to plant?
items.e: Equation: 6 475 + t = 10 000. Subtract 6 475 from both sides: t = 10 000 − 6 475 = 3 525. Check: 6 475 + 3 525 = 10 000. Wrong answers: 16 475 seedlings comes from adding 6 475 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Lwazi cuts a 200 cm cedar board into 8 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Equation: 8p = 200. 8p means 8 × p. Divide both sides by 8: p = 200 ÷ 8 = 25. Check: 8 × 25 = 200. Wrong answers: 192 cm comes from subtracting 8 instead of dividing; 1 600 cm comes from multiplying by 8 instead of dividing.

items.q: Kyle cuts a 200 cm cedar board into 8 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Equation: 8p = 200. 8p means 8 × p. Divide both sides by 8: p = 200 ÷ 8 = 25. Check: 8 × 25 = 200. Wrong answers: 192 cm comes from subtracting 8 instead of dividing; 1 600 cm comes from multiplying by 8 instead of dividing.

items.q: A square garden has a perimeter of 36 m. Use P = 4s to find the length of one side.
items.e: 4s = 36, so s = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 m. 144 m multiplies instead of dividing. 32 m subtracts 4.

items.q: Ravi’s sunflower is 4 cm tall. It grows 1,5 cm every week. How tall is it after 6 weeks?
items.e: 6 × 1,5 = 9 cm of growth. 4 + 9 = 13 cm. 9 cm forgets the 4 cm it started at. 11,5 cm counts only 5 weeks.

items.q: I think of a number. I multiply it by 3, then subtract 8. The answer is 25. What was my number?
items.e: Work backwards: 25 + 8 = 33, then 33 ÷ 3 = 11. Check: 11 × 3 = 33, 33 − 8 = 25. 5 23 subtracts 8 instead of adding. 33 forgets to divide. 67 works forwards: 25 × 3 − 8.

items.q: Tables are pushed together in a row. 1 table seats 6, 2 tables seat 10, 3 tables seat 14. How many people can sit at 8 tables in a row?
items.e: Each extra table adds 4 seats. The rule is 4n + 2: 4 × 8 + 2 = 34. 48 is 8 × 6, but tables pushed together lose the seats at the joins.

items.q: Using the same rule (4n + 2 seats for n tables), how many tables are needed to seat exactly 50 people?
items.e: 4n + 2 = 50, so 4n = 48 and n = 12. 9 divides 50 by 6, as if the tables were apart.

items.q: Pattern n of a tile design uses 5n + 1 tiles. Which pattern uses 46 tiles?
items.e: 5n + 1 = 46, so 5n = 45 and n = 9. Check: 5 × 9 + 1 = 46. 231 puts 46 in place of n. 9,4 adds 1 instead of subtracting.

items.q: Ayanda is a years old. Her sister is 3 years younger. Their ages add up to 21. How old is Ayanda?
An ice cream van has 4 flavours. Daniel chooses 2 different flavours for a cone. The order does not matter. How many different choices are there?
items.e: Call them A, B, C, D. AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD: 6 choices. 12 counts AB and BA as different, but the order does not matter.

items.q: Sarah buys x packs of 6 soccer cards and y packs of 4 cards. She gets exactly 26 cards. Which could be true?
Dumisani’s sunflower is 4 cm tall. It grows 1,5 cm every week. How tall is it after 6 weeks?
items.e: 6 × 1,5 = 9 cm of growth. 4 + 9 = 13 cm. 9 cm forgets the 4 cm it started at. 11,5 cm counts only 5 weeks.
